# Writeback unit {#sec-wbu .unnumbered}

## Goal for this week

- Know what the writeback unit (WBU) does for each kind of instruction
- Read its interface: the handshake with the Memory stage and the outputs
  that go back to Decode and Execute
- Understand why Writeback never stalls, and why its register write is
  qualified with the valid bit

## Introduction

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
- Last stage of HIPV: the instruction **retires** here
- The simplest stage: no memory, no FSM, no computation
- One job: write the result into the register file, **if** there is one
- What it writes depends on the instruction:
  - ALU result, loaded data, or `PC + 4`
  - or nothing at all
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
The writeback unit is the last stage of the HIPV pipeline. It is the place
where an instruction **retires**: its result becomes part of the
architectural state, the registers that a program can see, and the
instruction leaves the pipeline for good. After Writeback, the core is in
exactly the state that the algorithmic description of RV32I in the
[pipeline chapter](06-pipeline-structure.qmd) prescribes.

It is also the simplest stage. It talks to no memory, needs no FSM, and
computes nothing. Its one job is to write the result of the instruction
into the register file, if the instruction has a result. What that result
is depends on the instruction:

| Instructions | Written to `rd` |
|---|---|
| arithmetic and logic (`add`, `addi`, …), `lui`, `auipc` | the ALU result |
| loads (`lb`, `lh`, `lw`, `lbu`, `lhu`) | the data read from memory |
| jumps (`jal`, `jalr`) | the return address, `PC + 4` |
| stores, branches | nothing: they have no destination register |

Stores and branches pass through Writeback too. Their effects have already
happened, a memory write in the Memory stage and a redirect in Execute, so
in Writeback they do nothing except retire.
:::

## Interface of the WBU

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
| Group | Signals |
|---|---|
| Handshake with Memory | `ValidM` (in), `ReadyW` (out) |
| From Memory | `ALUResultM`, `ReadDataM`, `PCPlus4M`, `RdM`, `RegWriteM`, `ResultSrcM` (in) |
| Writeback outputs | `RegWriteW`, `RdW`, `ResultW` (out) → register file in Decode, forwarding in Execute |
| Retirement | `ValidW` (out) |
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
The WBU has the handshake with the Memory stage, the inputs from it, and
the writeback outputs:

```systemverilog
module wbu (input  logic        clk, reset,
            // handshake with the Memory stage
            input  logic        ValidM,
            output logic        ReadyW,
            // inputs from Memory
            input  logic [31:0] ALUResultM, ReadDataM, PCPlus4M,
            input  logic [4:0]  RdM,
            input  logic        RegWriteM,
            input  logic [1:0]  ResultSrcM,
            // writeback outputs (to the register file and hazard unit)
            output logic        ValidW,
            output logic        RegWriteW,
            output logic [4:0]  RdW,
            output logic [31:0] ResultW);
```

- **Handshake with the Memory stage**: `ValidM` and `ReadyW`.
- **Inputs from the Memory stage**: the three candidate results
  (`ALUResultM`, `ReadDataM` and `PCPlus4M`), the destination register
  `RdM`, the write enable `RegWriteM`, and `ResultSrcM`, which says which of
  the three results is the right one.
- **Writeback outputs**: `RegWriteW`, `RdW` and `ResultW` say *whether* to
  write, *which* register, and *what*. They travel back up the pipeline to
  two places:
  - to the **IDU**, where they drive the write port of the register file;
  - to the **IEU** and the hazard unit, where `ResultW` is one of the
    forwarded values, and `RegWriteW` and `RdW` decide when it is used.
- **`ValidW`** marks the cycle in which an instruction retires. Nothing in
  the core uses it, because `RegWriteW` already carries the valid bit, but
  it is a useful marker in waveforms, and the natural place to attach an
  instruction trace later.
:::

## Structure of the WBU

![The WBU: the valid bit (with `ReadyW` tied to 1), the M/W pipeline registers, the result multiplexer `resultmux`, and the AND gate that qualifies `RegWriteW` with the valid bit.](../images/blocks/wbu.svg){#fig-wbu}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
- **Handshake control**: `ReadyW = 1`, `EnMW`, valid bit `ValidW`
- **Pipeline registers**: `alureg`, `rdatareg`, `pcplus4reg`, `ctrlreg`
- **Writeback logic**: `resultmux` and `RegWriteW`
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
@fig-wbu shows the WBU. It has three parts:

1. the **handshake control**, which is especially simple here;
2. the **M/W pipeline registers**, which store the instruction coming from
   the Memory stage;
3. the **writeback logic**: the result multiplexer and the generation of
   the register write enable.
:::

## Handshake control

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
```systemverilog
  // writeback never stalls
  assign ReadyW = 1'b1;
  assign EnMW   = ValidM & ReadyW;

  // M/W valid bit
  always_ff @(posedge clk)
    if (reset) ValidW <= 1'b0;
    else ValidW <= EnMW;
```

- `ReadyW = 1`: the last stage has no one to wait for
- `EnMW = ValidM`: every valid instruction is accepted at once
- `ValidW` is loaded at **every** edge
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
```systemverilog
  // writeback never stalls
  assign ReadyW = 1'b1;
  assign EnMW   = ValidM & ReadyW;

  // M/W valid bit
  always_ff @(posedge clk)
    if (reset) ValidW <= 1'b0;
    else ValidW <= EnMW;
```

**`EnMW`** is the handshake between the Memory stage and Writeback: the
Memory stage offers an instruction (`ValidM`) and Writeback accepts it
(`ReadyW`). As in every stage, it is the enable of the pipeline registers.

**`ReadyW`** is constant 1. In every other stage, `ready` said "my own
instruction leaves at this edge, or I am empty". Writeback is the last
stage: its instruction leaves the pipeline after one cycle, unconditionally,
because there is no next stage that could be busy. The register file write
happens at the end of that cycle and always succeeds. So Writeback can
always accept a new instruction, and `EnMW` reduces to `ValidM`.

The **valid bit** `ValidW` follows the same idea in a simpler form. In the
other stages, it was loaded only when the stage was ready. Here the stage
is always ready, so it is loaded at every edge, with 1 when an instruction
arrives and 0 when a bubble arrives.
:::

## Pipeline registers

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
```systemverilog
  flopenr #(32) alureg(.clk(clk), .reset(reset), .en(EnMW), .D(ALUResultM), .Q(ALUResultW));
  flopenr #(32) rdatareg(.clk(clk), .reset(reset), .en(EnMW), .D(ReadDataM), .Q(ReadDataW));
  flopenr #(32) pcplus4reg(.clk(clk), .reset(reset), .en(EnMW), .D(PCPlus4M), .Q(PCPlus4W));
  flopenr #(8)  ctrlreg(.clk(clk), .reset(reset), .en(EnMW),
                        .D({RegWriteM, RdM, ResultSrcM}),
                        .Q({RegWriteWReg, RdW, ResultSrcW}));
```

| Register | Holds |
|---|---|
| `ALUResultW` | the ALU result |
| `ReadDataW` | the loaded data |
| `PCPlus4W` | the return address of `jal`/`jalr` |
| `RegWriteWReg`, `RdW`, `ResultSrcW` | whether, where, and what to write |
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
The pipeline registers are written at the handshake, on `EnMW`:

```systemverilog
  // M/W pipeline registers
  flopenr #(32) alureg(.clk(clk), .reset(reset), .en(EnMW), .D(ALUResultM), .Q(ALUResultW));
  flopenr #(32) rdatareg(.clk(clk), .reset(reset), .en(EnMW), .D(ReadDataM), .Q(ReadDataW));
  flopenr #(32) pcplus4reg(.clk(clk), .reset(reset), .en(EnMW), .D(PCPlus4M), .Q(PCPlus4W));
  flopenr #(8)  ctrlreg(.clk(clk), .reset(reset), .en(EnMW),
                        .D({RegWriteM, RdM, ResultSrcM}),
                        .Q({RegWriteWReg, RdW, ResultSrcW}));
```

- **`ALUResultW`**: the result computed by the ALU in Execute.
- **`ReadDataW`**: the word read from memory by a load, already shifted and
  extended by the LSU.
- **`PCPlus4W`**: the address of the next instruction, `PC + 4`, which
  `jal` and `jalr` write as their return address.
- **`ctrlreg`** packs the three control fields into one 8-bit register:
  `RegWriteWReg` (1 bit), the destination register `RdW` (5 bits), and
  `ResultSrcW` (2 bits), which selects which of the three results is
  written back.

Only one of the three results matters for any given instruction. The WBU
stores all three anyway, because it is simpler and cheaper to select at the
end than to decide earlier which one to carry.
:::

## Writeback logic

### The result multiplexer

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
```systemverilog
  mux3 #(32) resultmux(.D0(ALUResultW), .D1(ReadDataW), .D2(PCPlus4W),
                       .S(ResultSrcW), .Y(ResultW));
```

| `ResultSrcW` | Name | `ResultW` | Instructions |
|---|---|---|---|
| `00` | `RESULT_ALU` | `ALUResultW` | ALU, `lui`, `auipc` |
| `01` | `RESULT_MEM` | `ReadDataW` | loads |
| `10` | `RESULT_PC4` | `PCPlus4W` | `jal`, `jalr` |
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
The result is selected by a three-input multiplexer, the same generic
`mux3` as the forwarding multiplexers in Execute:

```systemverilog
  // result selection
  mux3 #(32) resultmux(.D0(ALUResultW), .D1(ReadDataW), .D2(PCPlus4W),
                       .S(ResultSrcW), .Y(ResultW));
```

The select **`ResultSrcW`** was decided long ago, in Decode, by the main
decoder, and has travelled with the instruction through three pipeline
registers. Its three values are the constants from `hipv_pkg`:

| `ResultSrcW` | Name | `ResultW` | Instructions |
|---|---|---|---|
| `00` | `RESULT_ALU` | `ALUResultW` | arithmetic and logic, `lui`, `auipc` |
| `01` | `RESULT_MEM` | `ReadDataW` | loads |
| `10` | `RESULT_PC4` | `PCPlus4W` | `jal`, `jalr` |

For stores and branches, the main decoder sets `RESULT_ALU`, but the value
does not matter, because these instructions do not write a register.

`ResultSrc` is used in two stages. In the Memory stage, `ResultSrcM` picks
`ForwardDataM` and identifies a load. In Writeback, `ResultSrcW` picks the
value that is written into the register file and forwarded from W.
:::

### The register write enable

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
```systemverilog
  assign RegWriteW = RegWriteWReg & ValidW;
```

- Enables the write into the register file
- `RegWriteWReg`: the instruction has a destination register
- `ValidW`: the stage holds a real instruction, not a bubble
  - after a bubble, the registers still hold the **old** instruction
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
**`RegWriteW`** enables the write into the register file. It drives the
write enable `WE3` of the register file in Decode, so a register changes
only when it is 1:

```systemverilog
  // register write, qualified with the stage valid bit
  assign RegWriteW = RegWriteWReg & ValidW;
```

It has two conditions:

- **`RegWriteWReg`**: the instruction has a destination register. This is
  `RegWriteD` from the main decoder, carried through the pipeline. It is 0
  for stores and branches.
- **`ValidW`**: the stage holds a real instruction.

The second condition looks redundant at first. `RegWriteM` coming from the
Memory stage is already qualified with that stage's valid bit, so a bubble
arrives with `RegWriteM = 0`. The catch is the enable of the pipeline
registers. When a bubble arrives, `EnMW` is 0, so `ctrlreg` is *not*
loaded, and `RegWriteWReg` keeps the value of the previous instruction,
which has already retired. Without `ValidW`, that instruction would write
its register again in every bubble cycle that follows, and would keep
showing up to the hazard unit as an instruction in Writeback.

In HIPV, this repeated write happens to be harmless: `RdW` and `ResultW`
are held too, so the same value lands in the same register, and the
forwarded value equals what the register file already holds. But it only
works by coincidence. It would break as soon as anything changed the
held values, and it makes every waveform misleading, showing writes that
belong to no instruction. Only `ValidW` knows whether the registers hold a
fresh instruction, so it is the right signal to qualify the write. The unit
testbench checks exactly this: `RegWriteW` stays low for bubbles.

The same pattern appears in every stage: a control signal that causes a
side effect, a register write here or a memory access in the LSU, is
qualified with the valid bit of its stage, because the contents of the
pipeline registers are meaningful only while that bit is 1.
:::

### Where the outputs go

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
- To the **IDU**: write port of the register file
  - `WE3 = RegWriteW`, `A3 = RdW`, `WD3 = ResultW`
  - write-first: the instruction in Decode sees the value in the same cycle
- To the **IEU**: `ResultW` is forwarding input `FWD_WB`
  - the hazard unit compares `RdW` with `Rs1E`, `Rs2E`
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
The three writeback outputs leave the WBU in two directions:

- To the **IDU**, where they form the write port of the register file:
  `RegWriteW` is the write enable `WE3`, `RdW` the address `A3`, and
  `ResultW` the data `WD3`. The register is written at the end of the
  cycle, and the write-first bypass in the register file lets the
  instruction in Decode see the new value already in this cycle.
- To the **IEU**, where `ResultW` is the `FWD_WB` input of the forwarding
  multiplexers. The hazard unit selects it when `RegWriteW` is 1 and `RdW`
  matches a source register of the instruction in Execute.

So the result of an instruction is available to the instructions behind it
from three places: forwarded from the Memory stage while it is there,
forwarded from Writeback one cycle later, and through the register file
from then on.
:::

## Summary

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
- The instruction retires: its result is written to the register file
- `ReadyW = 1`: the last stage never stalls
- `resultmux`: ALU result, loaded data or `PC + 4`, by `ResultSrcW`
- `RegWriteW = RegWriteWReg & ValidW`: bubbles never write
- Outputs go back to the register file (IDU) and to forwarding (IEU)
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
The WBU is the end of the pipeline, where an instruction retires. It never
stalls, so its handshake reduces to `ReadyW = 1`. It stores the three
candidate results, selects the one that the decoder chose with
`ResultSrcW`, and writes it into the register file in Decode, qualified
with its valid bit so that bubbles never write. The same three signals,
`RegWriteW`, `RdW` and `ResultW`, also feed the forwarding logic in
Execute.

This completes the five stages of HIPV. Each one has the same skeleton,
a valid/ready handshake with a valid bit and a set of pipeline registers,
and adds its own work: fetching, decoding, executing, accessing memory, and
writing back.
:::
